topic: Unlocking the Beauty of Euler's Formula: e^(πi) = -1
target_audience: High school students or curious learners with basic knowledge of trigonometry and complex numbers.

outline.topic: Unlocking the Beauty of Euler's Formula: e^(πi) = -1
outline.target_audience: High school students or curious learners with basic knowledge of trigonometry and complex numbers.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Complex Plane
sections.content: Introduce the complex plane where the horizontal axis represents real numbers and the vertical axis represents imaginary numbers (i).
sections.example: Visualizing a character moving on a 2D map: X-axis (Real) and Y-axis (Imaginary). A point 3+2i is just '3 units right, 2 units up'.

sections.title: The Meaning of i and Rotation
sections.content: Explain that multiplying by 'i' performs a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation. Repeated multiplication creates circular motion.
sections.example: An animation of a robotic arm rotating 90 degrees every time it gets 'multiplied' by i.

sections.title: Introducing the Taylor Series (The Engine)
sections.content: Briefly introduce the concept that complex functions can be expressed as infinite sums (Taylor Series) of simpler terms (powers).
sections.example: A 'building block' metaphor: Showing how stacking simple rectangles (polynomials) can eventually trace out a smooth sine wave.

sections.title: The Euler Identity Derivation
sections.content: Connect the series expansions of e^x, cos(x), and sin(x). Show how e^(ix) combines into a circular path on the complex plane: cos(x) + i*sin(x).
sections.example: A visual 'mesh' merging the graphs of sin/cos and e^x to show they overlap perfectly when i is introduced.

sections.title: The Grand Finale: e^(πi) = -1
sections.content: Set x = π. Show how the rotation on the unit circle lands exactly at -1 on the real axis.
sections.example: A 'Point-Runner' animation: A character starts at 1, travels along the arc of a circle for a distance of π radians, and stops exactly at -1.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: The complex plane has real and imaginary axes.
Think of points as coordinates on a map.
A point like 3+2i is easily plotted.

storyboard.title: The Meaning of i and Rotation
lecture_lines: Multiplying by 'i' rotates numbers ninety degrees.
This movement forms a perfect circle.

storyboard.title: Introducing the Taylor Series (The Engine)
lecture_lines: Complex functions can be infinite sums.
Taylor series use simple powers as building blocks.
Stacking these blocks creates complex shapes.

storyboard.title: The Euler Identity Derivation
lecture_lines: Series expansions of e^x, cos, and sin link.
Replacing x with ix merges these series.
Euler's formula connects exponentials to rotation.
This creates cos(x) plus i times sin(x).

storyboard.title: The Grand Finale: e^(πi) = -1
lecture_lines: Set the input x to pi.
Rotation of pi radians reaches the left side.
The result is exactly negative one.
e to the pi i is negative one.
